title: The efficiency edge: how the S1c < 600 phd boundary shapes inference at 250-270 keV and what an extended ROI would have shown
question: How does inference about the 248 keV event change if E_true = 262 keV, if the S1c edge (fixed in 2023) were 700-1200 phd instead of 600, and how does the edge shape the raster scan over delta (acceptance, fitted coupling, delta preference); what MSSI background would an extended ROI face in the 4.7 t FV?
headline_result: NEST-LZ MC reproduces the roll-off (E50 = 271.6 keV vs 269.9); the 600 phd edge accepts only 81/44/12/2.9% of the 1000 GeV O1 inelastic spectra at delta = 300/350/370/380 keV, so LZ's raster-scan couplings at delta >= 350 keV imply 1-30 unseen events in 600-1000 phd; with a 1000 phd edge (E50 = 423 keV, +0.003 NR-band MSSI events) the single-event Z(delta) peak moves from 380 keV (3.47 sigma) to 355 keV (2.89 sigma), Z(380) = 2.33 sigma, LR(380/300) 11.9 -> 0.48; E_true = 262 keV gives 1/eps = 1.26-1.40 and P(S1c > 600) = 17%
model_or_mechanism: nestpy GetQuanta NR fluctuations on P009's paper-contour scale + binomial S1/S2 detector model for eps_X(E) per S1c edge with S2c<10^4.15; WimPyDD O1 isoscalar inelastic (1000 GeV, LZ unit coupling, Baxter annual/June halos) over the full recoil window to 800 keV; P021 companion-free single-event profile q0 = 2[ln(f/b)-1+b/f] with kappa profiled; MSSI exponential/power-law interpolation between WS-ROI and HE-SB counts (4.7 t) with Fig. S4 NR-band fraction
stance: statistical reassessment (weakens the large-delta inelastic interpretation; neutral on the event)
confidence: medium: edge validated vs Fig. S2/P009, acceptance vs P015, Z vs P021 (<=0.11 sigma); MSSI interpolation (x1.8) and NR-band fraction (x4) are brackets; 1D observed-energy proxy
